You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. # - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed, with its actual front closure edges joined throughout and no remaining front opening?
node.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence establishes that the jacket's actual front closure edges are joined throughout the full closure and no opening remains. Fail when an identifiable opening between those edges remains at any section, even if another section is visibly closed. Compare corresponding closure-edge features across the source and edited images; distinguish the actual closure from the outer silhouette, projecting pink fabric, folds, sleeves, and bottom hem. Neither a broad pink flap nor the absence of a visible gap establishes full closure when the closure is concealed. Unknown when the closure cannot be located or traced sufficiently to establish completion, and no identifiable remaining opening establishes failure. A visible closed portion alone is insufficient for pass.
node.binding: Reference garment: the woman's pink jacket in the SOURCE image. Reference closure: its front panel edges bordering the visible dark central strip; use their relationship to the neckline and lower front of the jacket to identify the closure rather than treating the strip itself as a fastener. Evaluation target: the corresponding front closure of that same jacket in the EDITED image. Requested state: those front edges are joined throughout the closure, with no remaining front opening. Account for the woman's changed sideways pose when matching garment features. Do not substitute the projecting pink section, outer contour, or bottom hem for the closure; if the corresponding edges remain concealed or unidentifiable, retain unknown.

node_traces.evidence: In the source, the jacket’s front closure is identifiable around the dark central strip. In the edited image, the woman is turned sideways and a broad pink section projects outward; the corresponding closure edges are not sufficiently visible to trace throughout. The projection and lack of a clear gap do not establish that the jacket is fully closed, and no identifiable remaining opening is visible.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is already specific about the garment, source-to-edit correspondence, and pose change. The unresolved trace is a genuine visibility limitation: the edited jacket is turned sideways, and the projecting fabric does not reveal whether the actual closure edges meet throughout. Do not turn the reference label into evidence or force a yes; it constrains the aggregate, not the atomic visual judgment. For typed edits, preserve the decision role and completion criterion, but make the binding more operational about locating and tracing the corresponding closure in the edited view using visible garment landmarks, and distinguishing a concealed closure from an identifiable open section. Keep unknown when the edges cannot be assessed; do not infer closure from the flap, silhouette, or lack of a visible gap. The trace reports valid uncertainty with no transport, schema, or dependency failure, so changing execution plumbing is not indicated. Low coverage here is an investigation signal, not proof that the requested edit is absent."}
